picks.headline: Google's Flow Music adds song generation, editing and stem splitting to Spaces, its 'vibe coding' tool
picks.excerpt: Google has expanded its Flow Music platform, adding song generation, editing and stem splitting to Spaces, its 'vibe coding' tool. Musicians can now generate a song, replace a verse, separate vocals, extend a track and create album art, lyrics and video from one workspace, built on Lyria 3 Pro plus Gemini, Veo and Nano Banana.
picks.rationale: Google folds generation, editing, stem-split and art/video into one Lyria 3 Pro workspace — a major, credible new all-in-one AI studio that changes a producer's day-one workflow. Highest actionability + novelty.

picks.headline: Beatbox your ideas into reality with Vochlea's DubBox, an app that converts your voice into drum loops
picks.excerpt: Vochlea's new DubBox app uses machine learning to turn beatboxing into sample-based drum loops in real time. It learns up to eight of your vocal hits, triggers drum samples with velocity sensitivity, and uses 'Voice Warping' to time-stretch takes to the grid while preserving the feel of the original performance.
picks.rationale: ML that maps your beatboxing to velocity-sensitive, grid-locked drum loops in real time — a concrete new craft tool that changes how producers sketch rhythms. Novel release, reputable outlet.

picks.headline: Neutone and Roland's Project LYDIA lets you design your own AI models for real-time performance
picks.excerpt: Neutone and Roland are prototyping Project LYDIA, an AI effects pedal that lets musicians train, customise and hack their own neural-sampling AI models for real-time performance. 'You can open it up, you can hack it... you can really personalise it and make it your own,' says Neutone co-founder Andrew Fyfe — a hands-on, creator-owned take on AI as a live instrument rather than a black box.
picks.rationale: Creator-owned, trainable neural models on a hackable pedal — a fresh AI-as-live-instrument angle. Clears AI-craft relevance decisively; distinct from any published LYDIA/Neutone card.

picks.headline: Best stem separation tools 2026: 9 AI tools compared
picks.excerpt: MusicTech tested nine leading AI stem-separation tools and found results vary sharply by track and instrument: Logic Pro wins for fast everyday splits, while MVSEP edges ahead on critical vocals and hardest-to-isolate parts. A practical, craft-side map of where neural source-separation actually helps producers in 2026.
picks.rationale: Head-to-head of nine neural source-separation tools with per-instrument verdicts — directly actionable for a producer choosing a stem workflow tomorrow. Distinct from the published single-product zplane Peel Stems 2 card.
